rows.name: Cardio Thoracic & Vascular Surgery
rows.lead: Open-heart, lung and vascular surgery with a dedicated cardiac theatre and a post-operative ICU that never closes.
rows.intro_title: The surgery is planned long before the theatre doors open

intro_body.paragraph: Every case is discussed with the cardiologists first. Angiogram, echo and CT are read together, so a patient who does not need surgery is told that in the clinic rather than on the table.
Recovery is where cardiac surgery is won or lost. Patients come out of theatre into an ICU staffed by nurses who do nothing else, and physiotherapy starts on the first morning after.

badge.title: Vascular emergency?
badge.text: A cold, pulseless limb is time-critical — come straight to Emergency.

procedures.title: Coronary Artery Bypass
procedures.text: On-pump and beating-heart bypass grafting, planned with the cardiology team.

procedures.title: Valve Replacement
procedures.text: Mitral and aortic valve repair or replacement, mechanical and tissue.

procedures.title: Thoracic Surgery
procedures.text: Lung resection, decortication and chest wall procedures.

procedures.title: Aneurysm Repair
procedures.text: Open and endovascular repair of aortic and peripheral aneurysms.

procedures.title: Varicose Vein Surgery
procedures.text: Laser and conventional treatment for venous disease of the legs.

procedures.title: Congenital Heart Surgery
procedures.text: Correction of septal defects and other congenital lesions in children.

rows.conditions_lead: Chest and blood vessels — assessed jointly with cardiology, so surgery is offered only where it is the better answer.

rows.name: Cardiology
rows.lead: A round-the-clock cath lab, non-invasive diagnostics and a heart-failure clinic — under one roof, staffed by three consultants.
rows.intro_title: Every minute of a cardiac event is treated like one

intro_body.paragraph: Chest pain is triaged the moment it reaches our door. ECG within ten minutes, troponin at the bedside, and a cath lab team that is already gowning while the report prints.
Beyond emergencies, the department runs scheduled clinics for hypertension, arrhythmia, valve disease and post-bypass rehabilitation — so the care does not stop at discharge.

procedures.title: Primary Angioplasty
procedures.text: Emergency stenting for a heart attack in progress, available every hour of the year.

procedures.title: Coronary Angiography
procedures.text: Radial-access diagnostic imaging with same-day discharge for most patients.

procedures.title: Echocardiography
procedures.text: Transthoracic, transesophageal and stress echo reported by the consultant who scanned you.

procedures.title: Pacemaker Implantation
procedures.text: Single, dual-chamber and biventricular devices, with a lifelong follow-up clinic.

procedures.title: TMT & Holter
procedures.text: Treadmill testing and 24-hour rhythm monitoring booked within 48 hours.

procedures.title: Heart Failure Clinic
procedures.text: Weekly review, drug titration and fluid management to keep readmissions down.

rows.conditions_lead: If your symptom is on this list, book the cardiology clinic directly — you do not need a referral from another department first.

rows.name: Medicine
rows.lead: The department that sees you first when the diagnosis is not obvious — and decides which specialist, if any, you actually need.
rows.intro_title: Somebody has to look at the whole patient

intro_body.paragraph: Fever that will not break, weight that keeps falling, a cough into its fourth week — these do not arrive labelled with a department. Internal medicine is where they are worked up properly instead of being passed around.
The physicians also run the chronic clinics: diabetes, hypertension, thyroid and asthma, on a fixed follow-up schedule so a stable patient is not sent for the same tests twice a year.

checks.text: Referral only where it changes the plan

badge.title: Fever over five days?
badge.text: Book a medicine OPD slot rather than repeating antibiotics.

procedures.title: General Medicine OPD
procedures.text: A full history and examination, with the tests that follow from it and no others.

procedures.title: Diabetes Clinic
procedures.text: HbA1c-led review, insulin titration and foot screening on a fixed schedule.

procedures.title: Hypertension Clinic
procedures.text: Ambulatory monitoring, medication review and end-organ assessment.

procedures.title: Asthma & COPD Care
procedures.text: Spirometry, inhaler technique and a written action plan.

procedures.title: Fever & Infection Work-up
procedures.text: Structured investigation of prolonged fever, including dengue and enteric.

procedures.title: Inpatient Care
procedures.text: Ward and ICU management, with the same consultant through the admission.

rows.conditions_lead: If a symptom does not point clearly at one organ, start here. The physician decides what needs a specialist and what does not.

rows.name: Orthopedics & Spine Surgery
rows.lead: Joint replacement, spine surgery, sports injury and trauma care — with physiotherapy starting the day after surgery.
rows.intro_title: The operation is half the job — walking again is the other half

intro_body.paragraph: A replaced joint only counts once it is being used. Physiotherapy is booked before surgery, starts the morning after it, and continues as an outpatient course until you are back to your own stairs.
Trauma is covered around the clock: fractures are plated or nailed the same admission wherever the soft tissue allows.

badge.title: Free gait assessment
badge.text: Walk-in screening every Saturday morning, no appointment.

procedures.title: Total Knee Replacement
procedures.text: Navigated implant positioning, with a rehabilitation plan agreed before admission.

procedures.title: Hip Replacement
procedures.text: Primary and revision arthroplasty using cemented or uncemented implants.

procedures.title: Arthroscopy
procedures.text: Keyhole ACL reconstruction, meniscus and rotator-cuff repair.

procedures.title: Fracture Fixation
procedures.text: Plating, nailing and external fixation for trauma of any complexity.

procedures.title: Hand & Wrist Surgery
procedures.text: Carpal tunnel release, tendon repair and small-joint reconstruction.

procedures.title: Pediatric Orthopedics
procedures.text: Club foot, growth-plate injury and limb deformity correction.

rows.conditions_lead: Bone, joint, ligament and tendon — from a weekend sports tear to decades of wear.

rows.name: General & Laparoscopic Surgery
rows.lead: Keyhole surgery for gallbladder, hernia and appendix — smaller scars, shorter stays.
rows.intro_title: Keyhole wherever keyhole is the right answer

intro_body.paragraph: Laparoscopic surgery is the default here, not an upgrade. Three small incisions instead of one long one means less pain, a lower infection risk and most patients home inside two days.
Open surgery is still the correct choice for some cases, and we will say so plainly rather than convert halfway through for the sake of the brochure.

badge.title: Home in two days
badge.text: Typical stay for a keyhole gallbladder removal.

procedures.title: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
procedures.text: Keyhole gallbladder removal, usually discharged the next morning.

procedures.title: Hernia Repair
procedures.text: Mesh repair for inguinal, umbilical and incisional hernias.

procedures.title: Appendicectomy
procedures.text: Emergency keyhole appendix removal, theatre available at any hour.

procedures.title: Piles & Fistula Surgery
procedures.text: Stapler haemorrhoidopexy and fistula procedures as day cases.

procedures.title: Breast Lump Surgery
procedures.text: Biopsy, lumpectomy and mastectomy with oncology coordination.

procedures.title: Wound & Abscess Care
procedures.text: Drainage, debridement and diabetic-foot wound management.

rows.conditions_lead: Abdominal pain that will not settle deserves a surgical opinion — not another course of antacids.

rows.name: Gynecology & Obstetrics
rows.lead: Antenatal care, delivery and gynaecological surgery under one consultant — from the first scan to the first feed, and everything after it.
rows.intro_title: Nine months of care from the same faces

intro_body.paragraph: Continuity matters more in maternity than almost anywhere else. The consultant who confirms the pregnancy runs the growth scans, writes the birth plan and is called when labour starts.
A birth companion is welcome in the labour room. Ante-natal classes run every second Saturday and cover breathing, feeding and what the first fortnight at home is actually like.

checks.text: Growth and anomaly scans on site

badge.title: Labour room open 24/7
badge.text: Come in at any hour — no appointment needed in labour.

procedures.title: Antenatal Check-ups
procedures.text: Consultant-led visits on a fixed schedule, with growth tracked at every one.

procedures.title: Normal & Caesarean Delivery
procedures.text: Labour rooms staffed around the clock, with a birth companion welcome.

procedures.title: High-Risk Pregnancy
procedures.text: Diabetes, hypertension and twin pregnancies co-managed with medicine.

procedures.title: Laparoscopic Gynae Surgery
procedures.text: Keyhole hysterectomy, ovarian cyst and fibroid surgery.

procedures.title: Menstrual & PCOS Clinic
procedures.text: Investigation and long-term management of irregular and heavy bleeding.

procedures.title: Postnatal & Lactation Care
procedures.text: Review, contraception counselling and lactation support after discharge.

rows.conditions_title: What the gynecology team looks after
rows.conditions_lead: Pregnancy and everything outside it — the same consultant follows a patient through both, so the file never restarts.

rows.name: Urology
rows.lead: Endoscopic stone surgery, prostate care and reconstructive urology — most procedures done without a single open cut.
rows.intro_title: Most stones come out without opening anything

intro_body.paragraph: A stone is imaged, sized and located before anything is planned. Depending on where it sits, it comes out through the ureteroscope, through a keyhole in the flank, or is broken up from outside — open surgery is the last option, not the first.
The other half of the department is the prostate and continence clinic, where an enlarged prostate is measured rather than guessed at, and treated with drugs first where drugs will do.

badge.title: Cannot pass urine?
badge.text: Acute retention is an emergency — come in, do not wait for the OPD.

procedures.title: Laser Stone Surgery
procedures.text: Ureteroscopic and laser fragmentation, most patients home the next day.

procedures.title: PCNL
procedures.text: Keyhole removal of large kidney stones through a flank tract.

procedures.title: TURP
procedures.text: Endoscopic resection for an enlarged prostate causing obstruction.

procedures.title: Cystoscopy
procedures.text: Diagnostic and therapeutic bladder endoscopy as a day procedure.

procedures.title: Urethral Reconstruction
procedures.text: Stricture repair and urethroplasty for narrowed passages.

procedures.title: Uro-Oncology Surgery
procedures.text: Kidney, bladder and prostate cancer surgery with oncology input.

rows.conditions_lead: Kidney, bladder, prostate and the passages between them — in men, women and children.

rows.name: Nephrology
rows.lead: A 16-station dialysis unit running three shifts a day, with consultant nephrology cover for every chair.
rows.intro_title: Chronic care that fits around a working life

intro_body.paragraph: Dialysis is not a one-off event, it is a schedule someone lives with for years. We run early-morning, afternoon and evening shifts so treatment can sit around a job rather than replace it.
The general medicine side handles diabetes, thyroid, infection and the long tail of conditions that do not belong to any single organ specialty.

badge.title: Regular slot guaranteed
badge.text: Fixed weekly chair times for every long-term patient.

procedures.title: Haemodialysis
procedures.text: Bicarbonate dialysis on reverse-osmosis water, with single-use dialysers on request.

procedures.title: Peritoneal Dialysis
procedures.text: Home-based CAPD, including catheter insertion and family training.

procedures.title: Kidney Biopsy
procedures.text: Ultrasound-guided biopsy with same-day histopathology dispatch.

procedures.title: AV Fistula Surgery
procedures.text: Access creation and salvage, planned so it matures before you need it.

procedures.title: Diabetes Clinic
procedures.text: HbA1c-led review, insulin titration and foot screening in one visit.

procedures.title: General Medicine OPD
procedures.text: Fever, infection, thyroid, anaemia — the everyday work of a physician.

rows.conditions_lead: Kidney disease rarely arrives alone. Nephrology and internal medicine share a floor, so a single visit covers both.

rows.name: E.N.T
rows.lead: Endoscopic sinus and ear surgery, hearing assessment and a voice clinic — for patients from six months old upward.
rows.intro_title: A blocked nose for six months is not a cold

intro_body.paragraph: Long-standing nasal block, recurring ear discharge and a voice that has changed all get looked at directly — with an endoscope in the clinic, at the first visit, rather than after another course of tablets.
Hearing is measured, not estimated. Audiometry and tympanometry are in the same corridor as the consulting room, so a child suspected of glue ear leaves with a result the same morning.

badge.title: Sudden hearing loss
badge.text: Treated within 72 hours or not at all — come the same day.

procedures.title: Endoscopic Sinus Surgery
procedures.text: FESS for chronic sinusitis and polyps, through the nostril with no external scar.

procedures.title: Tympanoplasty
procedures.text: Microscopic repair of a perforated eardrum, with hearing reconstruction.

procedures.title: Tonsillectomy & Adenoidectomy
procedures.text: Day-case surgery for recurrent infection and obstructed breathing in children.

procedures.title: Voice & Laryngeal Surgery
procedures.text: Microlaryngeal surgery for nodules, polyps and persistent hoarseness.

procedures.title: Septoplasty
procedures.text: Correction of a deviated septum where the block is structural.

procedures.title: Neck Lump Surgery
procedures.text: Excision and biopsy of salivary, thyroglossal and lymph node swellings.

rows.conditions_lead: Ear, nose, throat, voice and the neck — for adults and for children, on separate lists.

conditions.text: Foreign body in ear or nose

rows.name: Neurology & Neuro Surgery
rows.lead: Neurologists and neurosurgeons on one floor — stroke, epilepsy and headache clinics alongside microsurgery and a neuro ICU.
rows.intro_title: Precision work, on the most delicate tissue there is

intro_body.paragraph: Neurosurgery leaves no margin for approximation. Every case is planned on thin-slice imaging, executed under the microscope and recovered in an ICU staffed by nurses trained only in neuro care.
Suspected stroke bypasses the queue entirely: CT within twenty minutes of arrival, thrombolysis decision made by the consultant on call.

badge.title: Stroke is time-critical
badge.text: Face drooping or slurred speech — come straight to Emergency.

procedures.title: Craniotomy
procedures.text: Tumour, haematoma and aneurysm surgery under the operating microscope.

procedures.title: Spinal Fusion
procedures.text: Instrumented fusion for instability, deformity and degenerative collapse.

procedures.title: Microdiscectomy
procedures.text: Keyhole removal of a herniated disc, most patients walking the same evening.

procedures.title: VP Shunt
procedures.text: Hydrocephalus management for infants and adults, with a programmable valve.

procedures.title: Nerve Decompression
procedures.text: Carpal tunnel, ulnar nerve and other entrapment releases as day surgery.

procedures.title: Head Injury Care
procedures.text: Trauma protocol from resuscitation through ICU to rehabilitation.

rows.conditions_lead: Brain, spine and peripheral nerve — assessed by the physicians and the surgeons together, so surgery is offered only where it is the answer.

rows.name: Gastroenterology
rows.lead: Endoscopy, liver care and GI surgery in one department — diagnostic scope in the morning, therapeutic list the same afternoon.
rows.intro_title: The scope answers in minutes what a scan guesses at

intro_body.paragraph: Upper GI endoscopy and colonoscopy run every working day, with sedation and same-day discharge. A bleed that arrives overnight gets scoped on arrival rather than at the next morning list.
Medical and surgical gastroenterology sit together. A patient with gallstones, a stricture or a suspected tumour is seen by both, once, instead of being referred back and forth.

badge.title: Blood in vomit or stool
badge.text: A GI bleed is an emergency at any hour — do not wait for the OPD.

procedures.title: Upper GI Endoscopy
procedures.text: Diagnostic and therapeutic gastroscopy, with biopsy where it is needed.

procedures.title: Colonoscopy
procedures.text: Full colonic examination with polypectomy in the same sitting.

procedures.title: ERCP
procedures.text: Stone removal and stenting for blocked bile and pancreatic ducts.

procedures.title: Liver Clinic
procedures.text: Hepatitis, fatty liver and cirrhosis followed on a fixed review schedule.

procedures.title: GI Surgery
procedures.text: Laparoscopic and open surgery for gallbladder, hernia and bowel disease.

procedures.title: GI Cancer Work-up
procedures.text: Staging, biopsy and multidisciplinary planning for digestive tract tumours.

rows.conditions_lead: Anything from the mouth to the anus, plus the liver and pancreas — investigated properly rather than treated as acidity.

rows.name: Plastic Surgery
rows.lead: Burns, trauma reconstruction, hand surgery and microvascular flap work — restoring function first, appearance alongside it.

intro_body.paragraph: A crushed hand, a burn contracture or a wound that will not close is a functional problem before it is a cosmetic one. The plan starts from what the patient needs to be able to do again.

Reconstructive work is staged and explained in advance — how many operations, how long between them, and what the result will realistically look like. Cosmetic procedures are offered on the same honest terms.

badge.title: Fresh burn?
badge.text: Cool with running water for 20 minutes, then come straight in.

procedures.title: Hand Surgery
procedures.text: Tendon, nerve and bone repair after crush and cut injuries.

procedures.title: Burns Management
procedures.text: Acute burn care, grafting and later release of contractures.

procedures.title: Wound Reconstruction
procedures.text: Flap and graft cover for diabetic, pressure and trauma wounds.

procedures.title: Cleft Lip & Palate
procedures.text: Staged repair for children, with speech follow-up.

procedures.title: Breast Reconstruction
procedures.text: Implant and flap reconstruction after cancer surgery.

procedures.title: Aesthetic Surgery
procedures.text: Scar revision, liposuction and rhinoplasty, with realistic counselling first.

rows.conditions_title: What the plastic surgery team handles
rows.conditions_lead: Referred from trauma, oncology and diabetes clinics as often as from the front desk — a wound that has not healed in six weeks needs an opinion.

rows.name: Maxillofacial Surgery
rows.lead: Jaw and facial trauma, impacted teeth, cysts and reconstruction — surgery on the part of the face nobody else covers.
rows.intro_title: The jaw is a joint, a bone and a bite all at once

intro_body.paragraph: A fractured jaw has to be fixed so the teeth still meet. Maxillofacial surgery is where facial trauma is plated, wired or splinted with the bite as the reference, not the X-ray alone.
The rest of the list is the work general dentistry refers on: impacted wisdom teeth, jaw cysts, salivary gland stones and implants placed into bone that needs grafting first.

badge.title: Facial injury
badge.text: Come to Emergency — a jaw fracture is best fixed within the first week.

procedures.title: Facial Fracture Fixation
procedures.text: Plating and fixation of jaw, cheekbone and orbital fractures.

procedures.title: Impacted Tooth Surgery
procedures.text: Surgical removal of wisdom and buried teeth under local or general anaesthesia.

procedures.title: Dental Implants
procedures.text: Single and multiple implants, with sinus lift or bone graft where required.

procedures.title: Cyst & Tumour Excision
procedures.text: Removal of jaw cysts and benign lesions, with reconstruction.

procedures.title: TMJ Management
procedures.text: Treatment for a clicking, locking or painful jaw joint.

procedures.title: Salivary Gland Surgery
procedures.text: Stone removal and gland surgery for chronic swelling.

rows.conditions_lead: Referred by dentists, by Emergency and by ENT — anything involving the jaws, the face and the mouth below the surface.

conditions.text: Mouth ulcers that will not heal

rows.name: Radiology & Imaging
rows.lead: Digital X-ray, ultrasound, Doppler and CT, reported by a consultant radiologist rather than by a technician.
rows.intro_title: An image is worth nothing until somebody reads it properly

intro_body.paragraph: Every study is reported by a radiologist, and a finding that changes management is phoned to the treating doctor rather than left in a queue. Prior films are pulled and compared before the report is signed.
Imaging runs alongside the clinics rather than after them: a patient sent from OPD for an ultrasound is usually back with the report inside the same visit.

badge.title: Reports on your phone
badge.text: Sent by WhatsApp the moment the radiologist signs them.

procedures.title: Digital X-Ray
procedures.text: Chest, spine and limb radiography with immediate digital review.

procedures.title: Ultrasound
procedures.text: Abdomen, pelvis, obstetric and small-parts scanning.

procedures.title: Colour Doppler
procedures.text: Arterial and venous studies for the limbs, neck and abdomen.

procedures.title: CT Scan
procedures.text: Plain and contrast studies, including emergency head and chest imaging.

procedures.title: Guided Procedures
procedures.text: Ultrasound-guided aspiration and biopsy, with pathology in the same block.

procedures.title: Bedside Imaging
procedures.text: Portable X-ray and ultrasound for ICU and immobile patients.

rows.conditions_lead: Most studies can be booked directly at the front desk with a prescription. Fasting and full-bladder instructions are given at booking.

rows.name: Pathology & Laboratory
rows.lead: Biochemistry, haematology, microbiology and histopathology in one block — most reports back the same day, delivered to your phone.
rows.intro_title: A result you can act on before the day is out

intro_body.paragraph: Waiting three days for a blood report delays every decision that depends on it. Routine biochemistry and haematology are released within six hours, and critical values are phoned to the treating doctor immediately.
Samples can be collected at home for anyone within eight kilometres — useful for elderly patients and anyone on a dialysis schedule.

badge.title: Reports on your phone
badge.text: Delivered by WhatsApp the moment they are verified.

procedures.title: Blood Chemistry
procedures.text: Liver, kidney, lipid and glucose panels with internal quality control on every run.

procedures.title: Haematology
procedures.text: Full blood counts, coagulation studies and peripheral smear review.

procedures.title: Microbiology
procedures.text: Culture and sensitivity for blood, urine, sputum and wound swabs.

procedures.title: Histopathology
procedures.text: Tissue diagnosis and reporting of surgical and biopsy specimens.

procedures.title: Cytology & FNAC
procedures.text: Fine-needle aspiration of lumps, reported by the pathologist who sampled them.

procedures.title: Home Collection
procedures.text: Sample collection at home within 8 km, with reports sent the same day.

rows.conditions_lead: Packages are priced as a bundle and can be booked without a prescription. Fasting requirements are texted the evening before.

rows.name: General Physician
rows.lead: The first door of the hospital — open six days a week, no appointment needed, for everything that has not been given a name yet.
rows.intro_title: Start here when you are not sure where to start

intro_body.paragraph: Most illness does not announce which specialist it belongs to. The general physicians see whoever walks in, work out what is actually going on, and treat it themselves where treating it themselves is right.

They are also the department that follows the ordinary things properly — a blood pressure that needs checking every month, a course of tablets that needs reviewing, a health check that needs explaining line by line.

checks.text: Walk-in consultation six days a week

badge.title: No appointment needed
badge.text: General OPD runs 9 AM to 8 PM, Monday to Saturday.

procedures.title: General Consultation
procedures.text: History, examination and a plan — with tests ordered only where they change it.

procedures.title: Health Check-up Review
procedures.text: Your package report explained line by line, with what to do about each finding.

procedures.title: Vaccination
procedures.text: Adult and travel immunisation, with a record card you keep.

procedures.title: Chronic Disease Follow-up
procedures.text: Monthly review of blood pressure, sugar and long-term medication.

procedures.title: Minor Procedures
procedures.text: Dressings, suturing, abscess drainage and foreign body removal.

procedures.title: Fitness & Medical Certificates
procedures.text: Pre-employment and fitness assessments issued the same day.

rows.conditions_lead: If it is none of the below, come anyway — sorting out which department you need is part of the job.

rows.name: Physiotherapy
rows.lead: Ward rounds every morning and an outpatient gym every afternoon — rehabilitation that starts the day after surgery, not the week after discharge.
rows.intro_title: Recovery is a course of treatment, not a leaflet

intro_body.paragraph: Every surgical and stroke inpatient is seen on the ward the morning after. Getting somebody sitting, then standing, then walking is what prevents the chest infections and the clots that follow a long lie-in.
Outpatient rehabilitation is booked as a course with a defined number of sessions and a measurable goal — range of movement, walking distance, or getting back to work — reviewed at the halfway mark.

badge.title: Free gait assessment
badge.text: Walk-in screening every Saturday morning, no appointment.

procedures.title: Post-Operative Rehab
procedures.text: Mobilisation, chest physiotherapy and strengthening after surgery.

procedures.title: Neuro Rehabilitation
procedures.text: Stroke, spinal injury and Parkinson rehabilitation on a structured programme.

procedures.title: Musculoskeletal Therapy
procedures.text: Manual therapy and exercise for back, neck and joint pain.

procedures.title: Sports Injury Rehab
procedures.text: Graded return-to-play programmes after ligament and muscle injury.

procedures.title: Electrotherapy
procedures.text: TENS, ultrasound and IFT used alongside exercise, not instead of it.

procedures.title: Home Exercise Planning
procedures.text: A written plan you can follow at home, reviewed at each visit.

rows.conditions_lead: Referred from the wards, from orthopedics and neurology, or booked directly — no referral is required for outpatient assessment.

rows.name: Dietetics & Nutrition
rows.lead: Clinical dietetics for inpatients and a weight, diabetes and child-growth clinic for everyone else.
rows.intro_title: A diet plan you can actually cook at home

intro_body.paragraph: A plan written around foods nobody in the household eats gets abandoned in a week. Ours are built from what is already in your kitchen, priced for your budget and written in the language you read most easily.
Inpatients are seen on the ward daily — renal, cardiac, diabetic and post-surgical diets are prepared in the hospital kitchen rather than outsourced.

badge.title: Free BMI screening
badge.text: Walk in any weekday between 10 AM and 12 noon.

procedures.title: Weight Management
procedures.text: Measured, gradual plans with fortnightly review — no crash protocols.

procedures.title: Diabetes Diet Planning
procedures.text: Carbohydrate counting matched to your insulin or tablet schedule.

procedures.title: Renal Nutrition
procedures.text: Potassium, phosphate and fluid targets coordinated with the dialysis unit.

procedures.title: Child Growth Clinic
procedures.text: Growth-chart tracking, fussy-eating support and anaemia correction.

procedures.title: Maternal Nutrition
procedures.text: Pregnancy and lactation plans built with the maternity team.

procedures.title: Inpatient Dietetics
procedures.text: Daily ward rounds and therapeutic meals cooked in the hospital kitchen.

rows.conditions_lead: Referral is not required. If any of the below applies, book directly at the front desk.
